propositions: The §I4a headline overstates the cascade guarantee; it must be narrowed from 'a child never runs ahead of its parent' to the per-edge, same-edge guarantee the _CASCADING_EDGES table actually enforces

A closed child reactivating to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade; this residual is documented-intended and does not violate the operator-ruled invariant that no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket

The blocked -> in_progress transition fires the start-work gate but does not cascade under an open parent; this non-cascading is reconciled as consistent with the gate's design when documented alongside the gate behavior

The store-level invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket' is maintained jointly by the two closed-source rows of _CASCADING_EDGES and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py, not by a total status ordering
No transition refused today becomes permitted by this reconciliation; the claim-status guard and _CASCADING_EDGES table rows remain byte-identical

Two pinning tests must document and verify the accepted residuals: that a blocked child resumed under an open parent does not cascade the parent, and that closing over a blocked child is refused by the unconditional close guard
